# 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.

**2** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, but not wholeheartedly.

**3** When the kingdom was firmly in his control, he executed the officials who had assassinated his father the king.

**4** Yet he did not put their children to death, following what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Parents must not be put to death for their children's sins, nor children for their parents' sins. Each person must be put to death for their own sin."

**5** Amaziah assembled the men of Judah and organized them by families under commanders of thousands and hundreds throughout Judah and Benjamin. He counted those twenty years old and above, and found 300,000 men ready for military service, able to handle the spear and shield.

**6** He also hired 100,000 experienced soldiers from Israel for 100 talents of silver.

**7** But a man of God came to him and said, "Your Majesty, do not take the Israelite army with you, because the LORD is not with Israel — not with any of these Ephraimites.

**8** Even if you fight bravely, God will overthrow you before the enemy. God has the power to help — and the power to overthrow."

**9** Amaziah asked the man of God, "But what about the hundred talents I paid for the Israelite troops?" The man of God replied, "The LORD can give you much more than that."

**10** So Amaziah dismissed the troops from Ephraim and sent them home. They were furious with Judah and left in a burning rage.

**11** Amaziah then took courage and led his army to the Valley of Salt, where he killed ten thousand men of Seir.

**12** The army of Judah also captured ten thousand men alive, took them to the top of a cliff, and threw them off. All were dashed to pieces.

**13** Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home raided the towns of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They killed three thousand people and carried off large quantities of plunder.

**14** When Amaziah returned from defeating the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people of Seir. He set them up as his own gods, bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.

**15** The LORD's anger burned against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him who said, "Why do you consult the gods of a people who could not even save their own people from you?"

**16** While the prophet was still speaking, the king interrupted, "Did we appoint you as a royal advisor? Stop — or you'll be killed!" The prophet stopped but said, "I know God has decided to destroy you, because you have done this and refused to listen to my counsel."

**17** After taking counsel, Amaziah king of Judah sent a challenge to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let's meet face to face."

**18** But Joash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son in marriage.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

**19** You think because you've defeated Edom you're something special. But stay home! Why ask for trouble and cause your own downfall — and Judah's with you?"

**20** Amaziah refused to listen — because God had determined to hand them over to their enemies for seeking the gods of Edom.

**21** So Joash king of Israel marched out. He and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other in battle at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

**22** Judah was routed by Israel, and every man fled home.

**23** Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem. He broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate — a section about six hundred feet long.

**24** He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in God's temple that were in Obed-edom's care, as well as the palace treasures and hostages, and returned to Samaria.

**25** Amaziah king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash king of Israel.

**26** The other events of Amaziah's reign, from beginning to end, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

**27** From the time Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem. He fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.

**28** He was brought back on horses and buried with his ancestors in the City of Judah.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **25:2**: "Not wholeheartedly" — three words that predict everything that follows. Amaziah's faith has an asterisk, and that asterisk will be his undoing.

- **25:14**: He defeats the Edomites, then adopts their gods. This is the most irrational act of idolatry in the entire Bible. You just proved these gods are powerless — and now you worship them?

- **25:15**: The prophet's logic is flawless: "Why would you worship gods that couldn't save their own people from you?" Amaziah's response is to threaten the prophet. When you can't answer the argument, silence the speaker.

- **25:20**: "Amaziah refused to listen — because God had determined to hand them over." The Chronicler reveals the invisible hand. Amaziah thinks he's making his own choice. He is. And God is using that choice as judgment.


— PNEUMA
